summary: H. A. Mullane played a match game of finger billiards at Murphy's saloon for a fifteen-dollar purse against five Jamestown gentlemen who were given cues. Mullane quickly cornered both reds and ran up fifty-two points before the crowd, finding the game stale, agreed to forfeit the stakes and let him give a free exhibition instead; no bets were laid during the exhibition, though Mullane made tempting invitations.
key_quotes: the flip fingered gentleman got the two reds in one corner of the table where he kept them until he had made fifty-two points
the most prominent feature of which was a paying quantity of suckers who would bet on 'another man's game'
